about: What the town holds in reserve, which of it could lawfully be spent on an operating deficit, how much goes in each year, and what the record cannot yet answer.

conclusions.basis: `stabilization_balances` for the balances; the general/restricted split is OURS, read off each fund’s name because the annual report prints a balance and never says what may be spent on what.
conclusions.claim: Only $3,147,179 of the $6,444,504 reserve may be spent on anything lawful.
conclusions.detail: The general fund takes a two-thirds Town Meeting vote. A special purpose fund created under c.40 §5B may be spent only on its stated purpose, and that purpose lives in the article that created it rather than in the fund’s name.
conclusions.not_shown: Whether a restricted fund’s stated purpose is narrow or broad. For four funds the creating article is not in this archive at all.

see.label: The same one-year problem, for free cash

conclusions.so_what: The other $3,297,325 is restricted to the purpose each fund was created for.

conclusions.basis: `town_meeting_votes`, classified from each article’s own subject line. Five sewer enterprise operating budgets mention a fund in passing and are excluded; counting them would overstate the money going in by more than the deposits themselves.
conclusions.claim: Town Meeting votes an average of $289,395 a year into these funds.
conclusions.detail: $4,051,527 in total since FY2012, and it is a FLOOR: 7 of the articles print no amount, including both of FY2025’s appropriations. $1,066,000 has been voted back out, and that is a floor too — money also leaves inside articles about something else.
conclusions.not_shown: How much of any balance’s rise is a deposit and how much is interest. The two cannot be separated here.
conclusions.so_what: Reducing a deposit is recurring money; spending a balance buys one year.

conclusions.claim: For 6 straight years deposits ran between $308,222 and $770,350.
conclusions.detail: FY2018 to FY2023: the consecutive years whose deposits exceeded the long-run average, found by walking the series rather than by choosing a window.
conclusions.not_shown: Whether the later fall is policy or a gap in what the warrant printed — some recent articles carry no amount.
conclusions.so_what: That run is what reducing the deposits would be worth against a gap.

conclusions.basis: `stabilization_balances`, ending cash at each proven year.
conclusions.claim: Vehicle/Equipment moved 40.8% a year; Zoning Incentive moved 0.8%.
conclusions.detail: Measured between each fund’s first and last PROVEN year, so the spans differ and each is printed beside its bar. It is the movement of a balance, not a rate of return.
conclusions.not_shown: How much of either movement is money voted in rather than interest earned.
conclusions.so_what: Two are being built; one is left alone to earn interest.
